section.name: Version Control
section.p: The Apache Tomcat project is in the process of migrating from Subversion to Git for version control. The following components use Git:

ul.li: Apache Tomcat migration tool for Jakarta EE

section.p: The following components currently use Subversion as the primary version control system:

section.name: Git
section.p: The ASF operates a dual primary system for repositories that use Git as their primary version control system. This means committers may commit to either gitbox.apache.org or GitHub.
For repositories that are mirrored to Git from Subversion, the mirrors may be found at git.apache.org or GitHub and are read-only for everyone.

section.name: tomcat.git
section.p: This is the Git repository that contains the Apache Tomcat source code. There are currently four branches:
master is the primary development branch. Apache Tomcat 10.0.x releases are tagged from this branch. Development work generally occurs in this branch first.
9.0.x is the stable release branch for Apache Tomcat 9.0.x. Generally, fixes are cherry picked from master into this branch.
8.5.x is the stable release branch for Apache Tomcat 8.5.x. Generally, fixes are cherry picked from 9.0.x into this branch.
7.0.x is the stable release branch for Apache Tomcat 7.0.x. Generally, fixes are cherry picked from 8.5.x into this branch.
A web based view of this repository is available via GitHub.

section.name: tomcat-connectors.git
section.p: This is the Git repository that contains the Apache Tomcat Connectors source code. This includes mod_jk and isapi. There is currently one active branch:

A web based view of this repository is available via GitHub.

subsection.name: Line endings
subsection.p: The repositories are configured so that when you check out from svn, you get the line ending appropriate for your platform for all files. The thinking behind this is that, for example, if you need to fix a typo in a .bat file from MacOS, it is easier if the .bat file has MacOS line-endings.

When you build locally, line-endings are not changed. The expectation is that the source has the correct line-endings for your platform so all the files that matter on your platform will have the correct line endings. When you are on Windows it doesn't matter if the .sh files have Windows line-endings since you'll never use them on Windows.
